subject: Commercial onramp commitments & decision checklist
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Elise Moran <elise.moran@unitri.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial onramp commitments & decision checklist

Hi Elise — great conversation today, thanks for carving out the time. Below is a concise recap of what we heard on the call, the proposed milestones for a 6‑week pilot, and the decision checklist that will help Unitri move to a paid Dedicated deployment if the pilot meets goals. Please confirm stakeholders and any changes to dates/owners.

Quick summary of pain & goals (what you emphasized):
- High false-positive rate on ticket triage rules when latency spikes (user impact during peak hours).
- Unitri needs predictable per‑incident cost and sub‑200ms 1st‑token latency for chat assist workflows.
- Security/compliance: must keep logs for 12 months, SSO + SCIM required, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Pilot objectives (success criteria):
1) Latency: median 1st‑token < 200ms at 95th percentile during simulated peak load.
2) Quality: > 10% reduction in false positives on the triage classifier vs. baseline within 4 weeks.
3) Cost predictability: per‑token unit cost estimate and forecasting dashboard visible to your engineering manager.

Proposed mutual commitments / milestones (timeline assumes kickoff Week 0 = Aug 3):
- Week 0 (Aug 3): Kickoff + environment access (API keys, test dataset snapshot, access to staging VPC). Owner: Unitri engineering (Elise).
- Week 1–2 (Aug 3–Aug 14): Integration + baseline collection (we'll run side‑by‑side with your staging traffic). Owner: Redwood (Camila) + Unitri (engineering).
- Week 3–4 (Aug 17–Aug 28): Optimization & tuning (batching, KV cache config, quantization suggestions). Deliverable: performance & cost forecast.
- Week 5–6 (Aug 31–Sep 11): Evaluation & handoff (final quality report, operations playbook, contract terms for Dedicated). Decision point: proceed to Dedicated or extend POC.

Procurement & legal asks you mentioned:
- SOC 2 Type II report + data retention policy (12 months).
- Standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and export redaction options.

Immediate next steps:
1) Please confirm the two procurement/legal contacts who need the SOC2/DPA packet.
2) Share a staging user with limited production traffic for baseline collection (we suggested a 48‑hour window of representative traffic).
3) I'll send a one‑page MAP (mutual action plan) that captures the milestones above, plus a short SOW draft and pricing for a 6‑week pilot.

Attachments (initial): Redwood_Security_Sheet_v3.pdf (summary SOC2 + data handling)

Thanks — I’ll follow up Monday morning with the MAP and a calendar invite for kickoff.

—
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifications and requests from my side: 

1) Procurement & legal contacts (looping them here): John Park (Procurement) and Maya Srinivasan (Legal). They will need the SOC 2 artifact and the DPA before we can kick off an environment that touches customer data.

2) Decision criteria: in addition to your three pilot objectives, Procurement will want a billing cap (we discussed a soft cap) and a proposed standard term for Dedicated (12 months minimum).

3) Timeline constraint: we have an internal release on Sep 6 that would benefit from successful pilot results — so if we can target final evaluation by Sep 3–10 window, that aligns well.

Please send the MAP + SOW + pricing so John and Maya can review. I'll arrange for a staging API key for a 48‑hour baseline period once we have the DPA in place.

Thanks — Elise
